q: Who was the first President of the United States?
fact: George Washington served as president from 1789 to 1797.

q: In which year did World War II end?
fact: World War II ended in 1945 with the surrenders of Germany and Japan.

q: Which structures at Giza were built by the ancient Egyptians?
fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely intact.

q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
fact: Apollo 11 astronauts landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

q: Who was the British prime minister for most of World War II?
fact: Winston Churchill became prime minister in 1940 and led Britain through most of the war.

q: Which ancient civilization built a famous network of aqueducts and roads across Europe?
fact: Roman aqueducts carried water into cities using gravity and carefully engineered slopes.

q: In which year was the United States Declaration of Independence adopted?
fact: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

q: The Great Wall was built to help protect which country from northern invasions?
fact: The Great Wall of China stretches more than 13,000 miles including all of its branches.

q: In which year did World War I begin?
fact: World War I began in 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

q: Who was President of the United States during the American Civil War?
fact: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863.

q: The ancient Olympic Games were first held in which country?
fact: The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, beginning in 776 BCE.

q: In which year did the Titanic sink on its maiden voyage?
fact: The Titanic sank in the North Atlantic Ocean in April 1912.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
fact: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 paved the way for German reunification in 1990.

q: Julius Caesar was a famous leader of which ancient state?
fact: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March in 44 BCE.

q: Johannes Gutenberg is best known for developing a movable-type printing press in which century?
fact: Gutenberg's press, developed around 1440, greatly reduced the cost of producing books in Europe.

q: Cleopatra was the last active ruler of which ancient kingdom?
fact: Cleopatra VII spoke several languages and ruled Egypt for more than two decades.

q: In which year did the American Civil War end?
fact: The American Civil War ended in 1865, the same year the Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery in the United States.

q: Alexander the Great was king of which ancient kingdom?
fact: By age 30, Alexander the Great had created one of the largest empires of the ancient world.

q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
fact: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 led to the Norman conquest of England.

q: The Magna Carta, which limited the power of the English king, was sealed in which year?
fact: King John sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215.

q: The Renaissance is generally considered to have begun in which country?
fact: Florence, Italy, was an early center of Renaissance art and learning.

q: Napoleon Bonaparte was finally defeated at which battle in 1815?
fact: The Battle of Waterloo was fought in present-day Belgium in June 1815.

q: In which year did the Wright brothers make their first successful powered airplane flight?
fact: The Wright brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk lasted only 12 seconds.

q: In which year did the Soviet Union officially dissolve?
fact: The Soviet Union dissolved in December 1991, ending the Cold War era.

q: The ancient Maya civilization developed mainly in which region?
fact: The Maya built major cities such as Tikal and Chichen Itza.

q: In which year was the United States Constitution signed at the Constitutional Convention?
fact: The U.S. Constitution was signed in Philadelphia in 1787 and ratified the following year.

q: King Henry VIII of England is famous for having how many wives?
fact: Two of Henry VIII's six marriages ended with the wife's execution.

q: Joan of Arc helped lead forces from which country during the Hundred Years' War?
fact: Joan of Arc helped lift the siege of Orleans in 1429.

q: Which empire came to an end in the aftermath of World War I?
fact: The Ottoman Empire had lasted for more than 600 years before it ended in 1922.

q: The Industrial Revolution began in which country?
fact: Britain's textile industry was one of the first to be transformed by machines and factories.

q: The California Gold Rush is generally considered to have begun in which year?
fact: Gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill in 1848, sparking the rush of 1849.

q: Leonardo da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, lived during which period?
fact: Leonardo da Vinci filled notebooks with studies of anatomy, flight, and engineering.

q: The Cold War was mainly a rivalry between the United States and which other power?
fact: The Cold War lasted from the late 1940s until the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.

q: Who became the first emperor of Rome in 27 BCE?
fact: Augustus, born Gaius Octavius, was the adopted heir of Julius Caesar.

q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
fact: The Berlin Wall stood for more than 28 years before it fell in 1989.

q: In 1803, the United States purchased the Louisiana Territory from which country?
fact: The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubled the size of the United States.

q: The Treaty of Versailles, which formally ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year?
fact: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on June 28, 1919, exactly five years after the assassination that helped trigger the war.

q: Constantinople was the capital of which empire?
a: The Ottoman Empire at its founding
fact: Constantinople was founded by the Roman emperor Constantine I in 330 CE.

q: Cuneiform, one of the earliest known writing systems, was developed by which people?
fact: Cuneiform was written by pressing a reed stylus into wet clay tablets.

q: The Wars of the Roses were fought between which two English houses?
fact: The Wars of the Roses ended when Henry Tudor became King Henry VII in 1485.

q: Ashoka was a famous emperor of which ancient Indian empire?
fact: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and promoted it across Asia.

q: The Meiji Restoration, which modernized Japan, began in which year?
fact: The Meiji Restoration restored imperial rule under Emperor Meiji in 1868.

q: The Battle of Agincourt in 1415 was part of which long conflict?
fact: English longbowmen played a decisive role in the victory at Agincourt.

q: Qin Shi Huang is best known as the first emperor of a unified what?
fact: Qin Shi Huang is buried with the famous Terracotta Army of thousands of clay soldiers.

q: The Rosetta Stone was key to deciphering which ancient writing system?
fact: The Rosetta Stone carries the same text in hieroglyphs, Demotic script, and ancient Greek.
